briefs.label: Morning Brief
briefs.title: Zalympix Trophies, JARS Goes National, and Psilocybin's FDA Fast Track
briefs.top: Michigan operators have real wins to point to this week — award-season bragging rights, a homegrown chain going national, and a governor's race where both parties are now courting the industry on tax relief. Nationally, the courts just backed federal rescheduling, Compass Pathways is closing in on an FDA filing, and M&A dollars are flowing again even as the DEA's final call on recreational cannabis remains the one thing everyone's still waiting on.

local.text: Mitten Canna Co. and Hytek crowned Zalympix champs — Michigan’s top cannabis growers have been crowned again, with Mitten Canna Co. and Hytek taking the biggest prizes at this year’s Zalympix, a high-profile competition often dubbed the “Grammys of Cannabis.”

JARS Cannabis becomes Arizona's biggest chain — JARS Cannabis and Sonoran Roots signed a definitive agreement for JARS to acquire Sonoran Roots, adding eight Ponderosa Dispensary locations to form a 27-dispensary statewide network, the largest retail footprint in Arizona.

Border towns outsell Detroit on rock-bottom prices — The average ounce here now runs about $60 compared with roughly $150 to $220 in Ohio and Illinois—which is why dispensaries in small border towns are now outselling those in Detroit.

GOP nominee courts industry with tax-repeal pledge — A trade association that represents marijuana businesses in Michigan is endorsing the Republican candidate in the state's gubernatorial election, calling him "the clear choice" due to his support for repealing or significantly rolling back a recently enacted tax hike on the industry.

State cracks down on mislabeled hemp concentrates — State regulators suspended a hemp processing license for the first time after regulators allegedly found three jars of potent concentrates at a Lansing-based Loud Labs—all of which tested well beyond the legal 0.3% THC limit that separates hemp from marijuana.

national.text: Federal court upholds medical marijuana rescheduling — On Sept. 9, 2026, the D.C. Circuit court left the medical marijuana rescheduling order in effect and held that the anti-rescheduling forces had not demonstrated a sufficient justification to stop the DOJ's rescheduling action.

Compass Pathways' psilocybin nears the FDA finish line — The FDA granted Compass's request for a rolling review, and in April 2026 the FDA issued a Commissioner's National Priority Voucher for COMP360 psilocybin treatment in treatment-resistant depression.

Curaleaf, Vireo ignite a $270M+ M&A wave — September 2026 cannabis M&A is defined by Curaleaf's unsolicited $270 million cross-border bid for Aurora Cannabis, and Vireo Growth's relentless acquisition campaign targeting roughly 270 dispensaries across Florida, Nevada, and beyond.

Congress buys the hemp industry more runway — Most of the federal hemp ban was delayed until December 11, as Congress gave the hemp industry a little more time after the House approved the Senate-passed Continuing Appropriations and Extensions bill.

Recreational rescheduling decision still pending — As of publication, on Sept. 11, 2026, no decision has yet been made by the DEA on whether recreational marijuana will be rescheduled, though a recommendation is likely to be submitted in late 2026.
